sections.heading: Going to Italy?
sections.body:
A few lessons before you go change the whole trip. You order at the trattoria, ask for directions, chat with the lady at the market, and people open up to you.

The lessons are online, built around the places you will visit and the words you will really use. And if you want, Valentina helps you plan the trip itself, with the places only Italians know.
sections.imageAlt: A narrow street in an Italian town

sections.heading: Taught by someone who learned by doing
sections.body:
Valentina is Italian. For twenty years she worked in fashion, traveling the world to train store teams, which is where she learned how adults really learn: by using the language.

Now she lives in Atlanta and teaches Italian and Spanish to adults, one to one and in small groups.

faq.q: Do I need to know anything before I start?
faq.a: No. Most students start from zero. Tell Valentina why you want to learn and she builds the first lessons around that.

faq.q: How often should I take lessons?
faq.a: We suggest two hours a week: enough to make progress, light enough to keep up.

faq.q: In person or online, which is better?
faq.a: Both work the same way. In person is nice if you are in Atlanta and have the time; online saves the traffic and lets you learn from anywhere.
Yes, children and teens too. Those lessons are planned together with the parents.
